newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on deliveries, technical.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on deliveries, technical.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on the posting again of heavy deliveries, weak stopping of those deliveries and on a continued technical slide, traders said.
Nearby November hit a session low of $6.59-3/4, near a one-year low of $6.59 set on November 14, 1995. New contract lows were set in soyoil and soymeal.

"The weather is bearish and yesterday's action was bearish," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. "Deliveries were the same but there were no good stoppers so this put pressure on the November."

There were 3.4 million bushels of soybeans posted Friday for delivery on the November which traders said were re-circulation of the soybeans posted Thursday. Thursday was first notice day for deliveries on the November.
Soybeans also were hit by weather and follow-through technical selling, the traders said.
"The weather is bearish and yesterday's action was bearish," Lespinasse said.
Soybeans closed one to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with November down 4-1/2 cents at $6.63-1/4.
Meteorologists said U.S. Midwest soybean producers would experience a cold weekend but warmer weather was expected next week amid generally dry conditions.
Soybeans fell Thursday on fund selling and prospects for USDA to hike its estimate for 1996 U.S. soybean production.
Soybeans found underpinning from good domestic and export demand plus talk China may be seeking U.S. soybeans and rumors China had purchased 15,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil.
Commercial buying in the soyoil pit helped escalate the China buying talk.

Technical indicators such as the key moving averages remain bearish while the short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November showed oversold signals. The RSI for November closed at 21 points, well below the generally perceived oversold level of 30.

Refco Inc sold four million bushels of January soybeans and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold four million March, traders said. Cargill Inc bought three million November and Smith Barney bought 2.5 million January, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 75,000 contracts, below 103,147 Thursday.

In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 1,500 March $6.75 puts and sold 1,500 March $6.50 puts at 11-1/2 to 12 cents, Cargill Investor Services sold 500 January $7.75 calls at 1-1/2 cents and Continental Grain bought 400 July $6.50 puts and sold 400 January $6.50 puts at eight cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, down from 26,755 Thursday.
